title: Author announces upcoming emulation technical articles
why: Announces planned articles on video emulation topics; contains no technical explanation of its own.

title: Objection to phone-number requirements in messengers
why: Personal distrust of phone-number signup; opinion without technical substance about Signal's protocol.

title: Estimates ignore engineers' variable mental state
why: Personal opinion on productivity variance; asserts the claim without much supporting analysis.

title: Insider view of Google's culture and freedom
why: Google's appeal is hard problems, smart coworkers and vast resources; flexible hours follow from trust, not perks.

title: Hydrogen cartridges versus lithium batteries energy math
why: Napkin math: a 5.5kg hydrogen cartridge matches about 24kg of lithium batteries for the same energy, but needs refuelling logistics.

title: Lymph is blood fluid cycling through tissues
why: Lymph is essentially blood minus red cells; fluid cycles like water, seeping into tissue and returned by pumping and muscle action.

title: Keto diet requires extra electrolytes to avoid cramps
why: Keto increases water and electrolyte loss; daily salt and magnesium supplementation is needed or cramps and deficiency symptoms follow.

title: Reasoning with depressed people is not effective
why: Personal and sensitive reflection on depression; no transferable technical lesson, and it responds to a thread-specific argument.

title: Opinion on Rust Belt cities and their identity
why: Cultural opinion about Midwestern cities and working-class identity; not an explanation a reader would learn from.

title: Partisan defence of a online harassment movement
why: Argumentative flame-war content that asserts claims about a contested political controversy.

title: Argument that languages should be editable by hand
why: Opinion essay arguing languages should be usable without IDE help; analogy-driven rather than a concrete technical explanation.

title: Layperson home-care advice during the pandemic
why: Unverified medical advice from a non-expert; not reliable enough to teach a technical reader anything.

title: Account locked out after losing two-factor phone
why: Personal complaint about support process; no general lesson beyond a frustrating anecdote.

title: Political critique of Australian encryption orders
why: Political rant about government overreach and charter rights; opinion rather than explanation.

title: Why Big Bang expansion is not inertia
why: Everything recedes in proportion to distance, so expansion must accelerate over time; inertia cannot produce this, so space itself expands.

title: Opinions on Go's assembler and linkers
why: Mostly rant and opinion about toolchain code quality; little concrete explanation of how the assembler works.

title: Opinion on killing local militia leaders in Iraq
why: Political and military opinion about US policy; argumentative rather than instructive.

title: Objections to inheritance-style voting model
why: Thread-specific commentary raising objections to a voting proposal; mostly opinion about political transparency trade-offs.

title: Gardening's hidden environmental costs: peat, plastic, water
why: Peat mining for compost damages carbon-storing bogs; plastic pots are unrecyclable; municipal water makes allotments costly.

title: Opinion on choosing boring technology for websites
why: Cultural opinion about engineers chasing new stacks; argumentative rather than a technical explanation.

title: Political rant on H1-B visas and outsourcing
why: Political opinion about immigration and jobs, lacking evidence and substance for a technical reader.

title: Personal account of quitting Facebook
why: Personal anecdote about social media habits; reflective but without a transferable technical lesson.

title: Opinion on Facebook centralising the web
why: Opinion essay about platform centralisation and browsers; no concrete explanation a reader would learn from.

title: Bootstrap maintainers announce leaving Twitter
why: Company and personnel announcement with no technical explanation.

title: Why insurance makes sense despite losing money on average
why: Insurance buys protection from ruinous losses; pay expected-value losses to cap worst cases, so insure only what you cannot afford to replace.

title: Personal account of Amazon's workplace pressure
why: Emotional first-hand account and venting about a company; no technical lesson.

title: Why x86 jumped to 64-bit: PAE and Windows
why: Windows XP lacked PAE support, so 64-bit became the path past 4GB; PAE alone would have let 32-bit systems address more memory.

title: Opinion on housing prices and foreign buyers
why: Political opinion about housing policy and San Francisco; argumentative, not explanatory.

title: Real-world tradeoffs of running Go servers
why: Go servers ran reliably, but garbage collection inflates memory under load, dependency management is hard, and vendor cloud libraries lag.

title: Cheap van-living setup without heavy investment
why: Used van, storage bins, a foam bed, inverter and marine battery suffice; the alternator charges it, so solar is unnecessary.

title: Company founder announces knowledge platform
why: Product launch pitch with goals and features; promotional rather than explanatory.

title: Opinion on online atheist communities
why: Personal opinion on religion and online communities; argumentative with no technical substance.

title: Request for a breakdown of longevity factors
why: A complaint about pop diet literature and a request for facts; asks questions rather than answering them.

title: Why Java's hello world is verbose on purpose
why: Java keeps all code inside classes and avoids top-level execution quirks, a design that helps large codebases despite verbose hello-world.

title: Commentary on a blogger's harassment case
why: Moral commentary about a specific person and online harassment; contextual and opinion-based.

title: Analogy about platform censorship and walled gardens
why: Metaphor-driven argument about YouTube moderation; opinion and rhetoric rather than explanation.

title: Argument for single-process deployments over containers
why: Opinion-driven argument about architecture preferences; anecdotal and not a substantive explanation.

title: What Windows 95 got right and what it missed
why: First release missed MSN and some networking, but the GUI redesign secured Microsoft's dominance; the Chicago reviewer guide lists its features.

title: Musings on ephemeral software engineering knowledge
why: Reflective opinion about culture and reinventing frameworks; questions outnumber concrete explanations.

title: Political argument about electoral college and Senate
why: Political argument about voting power and constitutional fairness; contested opinion rather than technical content.

title: Opinion on crypto's irreversibility and fraud risk
why: Critique of crypto transactions based on personal views; argumentative rather than a rigorous explanation.

title: Personal account of a game launch underperforming
why: Business anecdote about a game's sales; drama without a transferable lesson for a technical reader.

title: Why chip-making depends on deep specialised expertise
why: Chip design relies on specialised design software, skilled designers and about 40 process equipment types, each built on decades of expertise.

title: Insider history of Runescape botting arms race
why: A single developer's bytecode-binding bot repeatedly beat Jagex's obfuscation, and his web-walking API shifted the botting landscape.

title: Question about why fusion is only a matter of scale
why: Asks an open question with no answer in the comment; reader gains nothing by itself.

title: Why cheap burner phones still leave traces
why: Cell tower records, IMSI pings, SIM links to your account and purchase records mean a disposable phone is not untraceable.

title: Account of influencer prompting spam pull requests
why: News-style commentary about a viral incident and student mentorship; mostly reaction, not technical explanation.

title: The five-second test for landing pages
why: Show your landing page to people for five seconds; if they cannot state your value proposition, jargon is losing visitors.

title: How card fraud and chargebacks drive merchant freezes
why: US merchants bear chargeback liability, so fraud systems err cautious; stolen cards are used to buy from self-service merchants or cloned onto readers.

title: Personal account of schizoaffective disorder and work
why: Personal and emotional account of illness and workplace treatment; not a transferable technical or practical lesson.

title: Call to smash surveillance TVs in the street
why: Activist call to violence and rhetoric; not informative about how surveillance works.

title: Opinion on chatbots fooling people
why: Opinion piece about public perception of language models; argumentative rather than an explanation of the technology.

title: Alan Kay on bloated software complexity
why: Parc built the OS, language, apps and UI in about ten thousand lines by designing their own hardware, showing complexity is largely accidental.

title: Anecdote about a deli closing over wages
why: Local anecdote about a business and wages; observational opinion without a transferable explanation.

title: Hidden costs of four years of remote engineering
why: Remote work hides effort, isolates you, blurs home and work, and forces you to cover every role; first-hand and practical.

title: Story about a doorman and union elevator rules
why: Entertaining anecdote about building union rules; a story with no broader technical or practical lesson.

title: Founder launches Rewind product and funding
why: Product and funding announcement; promotional rather than informative.

title: Disputed claims about Chinese and US work culture
why: Contested cultural and economic generalisations argued in rebuttal; opinion rather than verifiable explanation.

title: Personal reflection on refusing Facebook data sharing
why: Personal anecdote about privacy and relationships; reflective opinion with no concrete technical lesson.

title: Opinion on whether Hacker News is healthy
why: Opinion about community quality and demographics; subjective and about the site itself.

title: Swapping MacBook optical drive for SSD: practical tips
why: Install Boot Camp before removing the optical drive; the optical bay is slower, so put the SSD there; battery life barely changes.

title: Advice on software engineers and business ownership
why: Career opinion advocating founding businesses over coding; persuasive rather than explanatory.

title: Starting audio programming with WebAudio and Tone.js
why: WebAudio offers oscillators and filters, Tone.js simplifies it, and AudioWorklet enables custom DSP, with browser performance limits.

title: How Latin word order mirrors meaning in verse
why: Flexible Latin word order lets poets place words to mirror content, such as isolating exilium to evoke exile, a technique Ovid uses masterfully.

title: Experience of Haskell tooling problems on Windows
why: Frustration report about Cabal and Windows dependencies; personal complaint rather than a reusable explanation.

title: How writing-style fingerprinting identifies authors
why: Frequencies of near-synonym word choices give small per-marker information that accumulates into an author profile; Mosteller and Wallace pioneered it.

title: Why CS study builds invariant-maintaining thinking
why: CS education cultivates reasoning about invariants and API constraints that self-taught programmers often lack, leading to sloppy use of constrained APIs.

title: Experience of iPad usability regressions
why: Personal critique of Apple's UI decisions with a list of complaints; opinion rather than explanation.

title: Question about meditation and hallucinations
why: A personal seeker's question about meditation experiences; asks for guidance rather than explaining anything.

title: Solar's real share of US electricity is small
why: Solar supplied about 1.3% of US electricity; 'biggest new source' headlines reflect new capacity, while gas drove coal's decline.

title: Running your own mail server is simpler than assumed
why: Postfix plus postgrey and spam filtering on a Debian box gives you owned email; the difficulty is mostly perceived rather than real.

title: Blog traffic patterns from ten years of logs
why: Most posts get single-digit views; Reddit or HN spikes fade within days with no retention, and RSS is rarely used.

title: Large tech codebases as old cities
why: Long-lived tech companies grow like old cities, with layered and adapted systems no one fully understands, so nobody can say where all data lives.

title: Defence of China's internet firewall
why: Political argument for protectionism and against foreign platforms; opinion rather than technical or factual explanation.

title: Why lifetime 'unlimited' perks signal financial trouble
why: Fixed-fee lifetime perks often precede bankruptcy; free perks distort behaviour, so incentives should be paid per use, not as flat fees.

title: How sodium or lithium-sulfur battery discharge works
why: Metal anodes push electrons down the wire and ions into the glass electrolyte; ion buildup chokes the flow, which is what limits discharge.

title: Solo developer's enthusiasm for Kubernetes
why: Personal endorsement of Kubernetes with a learning path; enthusiastic opinion more than a concrete explanation.

title: Caution against ADHD self-diagnosis trends
why: Opinion on pop-culture ADHD quizzes and mentoring experience; sensible but general, without a concrete technical lesson.

title: NYT sells ads targeted by predicted reader feelings
why: NYT predicts reader emotions per article; most predicted feelings are positive, and emotional targeting raised per-ad revenue by up to 80%.

title: Rebuttal of economists' account of trade debates
why: Political argument about free markets versus intervention and economists' narratives; contested opinion rather than explanation.

title: Practical advice for going blind as a developer
why: Learn NVDA or VoiceOver, use the keyboard only, accept inaccessible tools, and use the command line where GUIs fail.

title: Why GPL doesn't require releasing training code
why: Weights shipped with a GPL program don't oblige releasing the training code; training procedures are separate from the distributed program.

title: Complaint about shoddy online systems in the pandemic
why: Opinion calling for software standards after outages; argumentative with no specific technical explanation.

title: Opinion on Google+ real names and speech
why: Personal political and social opinion about real-name policies; argumentative rather than instructive.

title: Describes personal browser extension for HN search
why: Describes a moderator's personal workflow and tool; interesting but offers little general technique to learn.

title: Why luxury engines use cheap, failure-prone parts
why: Plastic oil filter modules and plastic cooling systems often fail, and cheap bearings wear out, so luxury cars need frequent service.

title: Opinion on Rust's maintainability versus Go
why: Opinion on language ecosystems and predictions about the future; argumentative rather than explanatory.

title: Anecdote about Gandi and suspected domain sniping
why: Personal suspicion about domain sniping and a company's trustworthiness; anecdotal with no verified technical lesson.

title: Author defends Julia Brainfuck transpiler benchmarks
why: Shows a benchmark of a personal transpiler and argues about methodology; too context-dependent for a standalone lesson.

title: How brokerage settlement float and clearing work
why: Sales take about two days to clear, so brokers fund trades from a float pool; that pool's depletion creates systemic risk.

title: Personal dating data about ethnicity and matches
why: Anecdotal dating experience with a personal tally; a single observer's data without rigorous method.

title: Anecdote on overengineered quadratic-solver libraries
why: Opinion and anecdote about overengineering; the lesson is valid but argued through a single personal story.

title: Personal switch back to Firefox for privacy
why: User preference and anecdote about browsers and video performance; opinion without a technical explanation.

title: Reflection on YouTube's cultural importance
why: Reflective essay on YouTube's place in society; philosophical musing without concrete knowledge to learn.

title: Hidden work involved in listing and selling a house
why: Every listing repeats inspections, radon tests, showings, staging, repairs negotiation and disclosures; much of this recurs each time a home is relisted.

title: Argument that gold beats stocks over time
why: Investment opinion with selectively chosen returns; advocacy rather than balanced explanation.

title: How opt-out and objection work in class actions
why: App developers are automatically in the class unless they opt out within 105 days; objecting or excluding determines whether they are bound.

title: Anecdote about fraudulent research and a recommended book
why: Anecdote about a fraudulent researcher and a book recommendation; mostly story and opinion without a method to learn.
